question: Am I eligible to volunteer?
answer: You must be over 18 years old and able to volunteer consistently for at least 6 months, committing at least 4 hours per week. You must also spend at least 20 minutes weekly catching up and communicating with volunteers and trainees on Slack. Volunteers must follow the CYF Code of Conduct, Volunteer Agreement, values and working principles. There is flexibility for holidays and other circumstances.
review_notes: Reviewed against the CYF Volunteer FAQ.

question: Can I volunteer without professional experience?
answer: Yes. You can support Intro to Digital and Basic Online Skills courses even if you do not have professional experience. CYF also welcomes volunteers without a technical background because trainees need support with a wide range of professional skills.

question: I signed up to volunteer. What happens next?

question: How can I help as a volunteer?
answer:
CodeYourFuture offers different volunteering opportunities depending on your professional experience, availability, and interests.

When choosing a role, consider:
- Whether you prefer volunteering remotely or in person.
- Whether you can commit at least 4 hours per week.
- Whether you are available on weekdays or Saturdays.
- Your professional experience.

Volunteers with less than 2 years of professional experience:
- Class Facilitator: Support Basic Online Skills or Intro to Digital sessions.
- Coursework Reviewer: Review Basic Online Skills submissions or Intro to Digital exercises.

Volunteers with 2–5 years of professional experience:
- Class Facilitator: Support Intro to Programming classes.
- Career Mentor: Support trainees with career development.
- Employability Reviewer: Review CVs, conduct mock interviews, or provide presentation feedback.
- Pair Programmer: Work individually with trainees to develop technical skills.
- Code Reviewer: Review trainee pull requests and provide feedback.

Volunteers with more than 5 years of professional experience:
- Class Facilitator: Support Software Development Course classes, either in person or remotely.
- Code Reviewer: Review trainee pull requests and provide feedback.

Other opportunities include:
- Community event management.
- Marketing and communications.
- Outreach, partnerships, and speaking at events.

Some roles have additional expectations, such as reviewing approximately 10 pull requests per week.

The most suitable opportunity depends on your experience, availability, and the needs of CodeYourFuture.

question: What courses do you have?
answer:
CodeYourFuture offers two main learning programmes:

1. Basic Online Skills
A free, hands-on three-week course that helps learners use smartphones and other devices, manage apps and files, and stay safer online.

More information:
https://codeyourfuture.io/dds/

2. Software Development Course pathway
This pathway includes several stages:

- Intro to Digital: An introduction to essential digital skills.
- Intro to Programming: The next stage after passing the eligibility check.
- Checkpoint: Follows Intro to Programming after passing a technical test.
- Software Development Course: Follows successful completion of Checkpoint assignments.
- Job search: Trainees completing the Software Development Course can progress towards engineering opportunities. The pathway also shows an entry-level tech job-search route for learners who do not continue after Intro to Programming.

Course information:
- Intro to Digital: https://itd.codeyourfuture.io/
- Intro to Programming: https://programming.codeyourfuture.io/
- Checkpoint: https://checkout.codeyourfuture.io/
- Software Development Course: https://sdc.codeyourfuture.io/

Volunteer opportunities may involve supporting learners at different stages of these programmes.

question: What knowledge do I need to have for each course?
answer:
CodeYourFuture welcomes volunteers from different professional backgrounds. You do not need to be an expert in every tool or programming language to support a class.

The knowledge and experience expected depend on the course:

Intro to Digital
- Suggested experience: Less than 2 years of professional experience.
- Tools: Slack, AI tools, and Google Sheets.
- Technical topics: HTML and CSS.

Intro to Programming
- Suggested experience: At least 2 years of professional experience.
- Professional skills: Time management, presentations, job searching, and planning.
- Technical topics: JavaScript and HTML.

Checkpoint
- Participation is by invitation only.
- The supplied FAQ does not specify the knowledge required for volunteers.

Software Development Course
- Suggested experience: More than 5 years of professional experience.
- Professional skills: Time management, presentations, job searching, and planning.
- Technical knowledge: Enough experience to support trainees with JavaScript questions.

These descriptions are taken from the supplied Volunteer FAQ and may need confirmation against current CodeYourFuture volunteering requirements.

question: What teaching method do you use?
answer:
CodeYourFuture uses the flipped classroom model. Trainees are expected to prepare independently before attending classes and take responsibility for their learning.

Classes are not traditional lectures. Instead, volunteers and trainees use their time together for practical activities such as debugging, pair programming, code reviews, and building projects.

The aim is to help trainees overcome challenges, collaborate, and develop skills through practical experience.

You can learn more about the flipped classroom here: https://youtu.be/r2b7GeuqkPc

question: Tell me about the onboarding process
answer:
These are steps for onboarding:
1. Sign-up
2. Receive sign-up confirmation email with link for first session
3. Welcome Session: find out more about CYF
4. Receive an email with a presentation and quiz, sign the Volunteer agreement, read about our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies
5. Receive an invite to our Slack workspace
6. Introduce yourself on the channel #cyf-volunteers
7. Do the relevant trainings (Edu Training, Tools Training, Code review training, etc)
8. Come to the nearest class to you to get to know people
9. Watch our Slack Essentials at CYF video
10. Start contributing

question: What is Slack and how does it work?
answer:
Slack is the operating system that brings people together. And because we all just meet on Saturdays, we need a way of talking to each other during the week too. Slack is that place.
Slack is also a software used actively in the tech industry for communication. So by learning how to use it, you’ll already know how to get around it on your first job.
Our Slack is organised as follows:
Intro to Digital and Basic Online Skills workspace
CYF Community workspace: includes all trainees and volunteers
All workspaces have the same channel structure, so search for keywords such as your region i.e. “London” and find the channels that you’d like to join, for example, #london-community
Our automated workflows will invite you to the most important channels, but some channels might be missing, so join them yourself.

question: Where do I send my feedback to?
answer:
The answer depends on what type of feedback.
If it's something related to you to make your community better, share it on Slack or during a class with the community. Sharing what is going well or isn’t going well is very important to make your day-to-day better.
If your feedback is something direct to one person (trainee, volunteers, staff), we suggest you talk to them directly. We suggest using the SBI feedback model (Situation, Behaviour, Impact) to do so.

question: Who can help me with a referral or reference letter?
answer:
Once you have completed 12 months of volunteering at least 4 hours a week at CodeYourFuture, we’ll happily provide you with a reference letter (for example, for a job application, a visa, or a course).
These letters use a template in which we state which region you are in, what type of volunteering you supported us with, and explain CYF and the impact.
To request this, please fill in this form:
👉 Request a Reference or Letter of Support
Tell us what you need and why. This helps us write the right letter for you.
Please allow enough time before your deadline. We will take up to 5 working days to reply to you.

question: I want to introduce CYF to my company
answer:
That’s fantastic news. Our suggested steps are:
1. Identify the highest level in your organisation that you would feel comfortable introducing us to. This can be the CEO, CTO, VP, Director or other role
2. Send them an email introducing CYF and Jemima and German - make sure you copy them into it
1. jemima AT code.yourfuture.io
2. german AT codeyourfuture.io (substitute AT by @) on the email
Suggested email: “I have been volunteering for CodeYourFuture (CYF), an organisation with the mission to move those from marginalised communities into employment.
CYF helps reduce the company's hiring risk: their engineers have rigorous training, employability support and recruitment turns into an efficient and successful process.
I have been impressed with the calibre of talent at CYF. I’d like to introduce you to the CEO/Founder, Germán Bencci, to explore whether we could benefit from partnering with CYF.”
